title: Merge Strategies & Conflict Resolution
notes: Exceptional performance on merge strategies and conflict resolution. Demonstrated advanced systems thinking by independently deriving Single Responsibility Principle when analyzing conflict scenarios. Successfully completed intentional conflict creation/resolution exercise. Identified critical post-merge ritual as muscle-memory priority. Articulated profound mental model shift from collaborative development feeling like 'tangled web' to structured, manageable process. Strong grasp of three merge strategies (merge commit, squash, rebase), conflict marker anatomy, VS Code conflict resolution tools, GitHub PR merge interface, and complete branch cleanup workflows.
strengths: First-principles reasoning (derived SRP without prior exposure)
Synthesis over binary choices in conflict resolution
Systems thinking (housekeeping, risk assessment, forward planning)
Practical judgment (when to use merge commit vs squash)
areas_for_growth: Post-merge ritual needs repetition to become automatic
Merge conflict resolution needs more practice (acknowledged by learner)
Testing after merge (concept understood, needs to become habit)
key_takeaways: Squash-and-merge is default for CatchBook feature branches (clean history)
Merge conflicts aren't disasters—they're decision points requiring synthesis
VS Code conflict resolution UI significantly reduces cognitive load
Git collaboration is structured, not chaotic—merges happen one at a time
next_steps: Continue to P01-M03-L01 (Introduction to Conventional Commits). Will build on merge workflow knowledge with professional commit message standards.
